author: s. v. diaz
title: Cal Poly men's basketball faces UC Santa Barbara before hosting Cal State Fullerton
text:
The Cal Poly men’s basketball team is set for two key matchups this week, facing UC Santa Barbara on Thursday and Cal State Fullerton on Saturday. The Mustangs currently stand eighth in the Big West with a 7-12 overall record and a 3-4 mark in conference play. They trail joint conference leaders Hawai’i and UC Irvine by just two games.
UC Santa Barbara, which shares third place in the standings, has won its last 16 meetings against Cal Poly. The Gauchos lead the all-time series 86-35, including a 52-14 advantage since both programs joined Division I. Cal Poly last beat UC Santa Barbara at home in January 2018.
Against Cal State Fullerton, Cal Poly holds a slight edge historically (42-39) and has won three straight, including a high-scoring road victory earlier this season.
Cal Poly continues to rank among the top NCAA Division I teams for three-point shooting attempts and makes per game. The Mustangs are averaging over ten made threes per contest, ranking tenth nationally in attempts and fourteenth in total three-pointers made.
Sophomore guard Hamad Mousa leads the Big West with an average of 21.6 points per game, also placing eleventh nationally. He has reached double figures in every appearance this season and posted a career-high 34 points against CSUN earlier this month. Mousa also ranks seventh among conference players for free throw percentage and sixth for rebounds per game.
Cayden Ward, another sophomore guard, is second on the team with an average of 15 points per game after earning Big West Player of the Week honors following his career-best performance at Utah.
Peter Bandelj remains one of the Mustangs’ key contributors as well, coming off a program-record nine three-pointers against Cal State Fullerton. Bandelj averages nearly fifteen points per game and maintains strong marks from beyond the arc and at the free throw line.
This year’s roster includes players from nine different countries—more than most other Division I teams—and covers all six habitable continents or regions.
During the offseason, Cal Poly was one of only five Division I programs not to lose any players to the transfer portal.
On October 22nd, former Mustang Kobe Sanders became just the second alum from Cal Poly to appear in an NBA game when he played for the Los Angeles Clippers after being drafted by New York Knicks and traded over. Sanders joins David Nwaba as one of two former Mustangs to have played professionally in the league.
The Mustangs are competing in their thirty-second season at the Division I level and eighty-second as a four-year program.
